notes.note: Filming subjects is routine in exercise science research; prior studies recorded lifters' bench press and squat sets on video to analyze range of motion and technique. What's actually new here is public release of anonymized footage, not permission to film.
notes.claim: The range of motion study Jeff Nippard was involved with in New York was the first exercise science study where the researchers were allowed to film the subjects.
notes.context_quote: The range of motion study that I did last year in New York comparing full range of motion to lengthen partials was actually the first ever exercise science study where the researchers were allowed to film the subjects.
notes.context_paragraph: The range of motion study that I did last year in New York comparing full range of motion to lengthen partials was actually the first ever exercise science study where the researchers were allowed to film the subjects. And even with that permission, we still had to blur out their faces.

sources.quote: Time under tension was obtained manually from the data recorded by a camera (Sony FDR191 AX53), using slow-speed playback (1/5 speed).
sources.explanation: This demonstrates that filming subjects to analyze resistance training (specifically bench press) is a documented practice in previous research, contradicting the claim that it was prohibited until recently.

sources.quote: They observed videos of two trainees completing sets of the barbell bench press and barbell back squat exercises, using three loads (45%, 65%, and 85% of 1 repetition-maximum [1RM]), and recorded from two views (front and side).
sources.explanation: This shows a prior study where researchers recorded videos of participants performing the exact exercises mentioned (squats and bench press) for analysis.

sources.quote: In this within-participant study, thirty healthy, resistance-trained participants had their upper extremities randomly assigned to either a lengthened partial or full ROM condition
sources.explanation: This confirms the specific study being discussed in the post (Wolf et al. 2025 regarding lengthened partials vs full ROM).
